mainEntity.name: What types of electrical services do you offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: From entire remodels to small repairs, we do it all. Visit our services page or give us a call at 602-769-7892.

If you don't see your city listed, give us a call and we'll let you know if you're in our service radius.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer free estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes we do! We'll come out, look at the job, and give you a straight answer on what it'll cost. No pressure and no obligation. Contact us today to get a free quote.

mainEntity.name: I want to upgrade my lighting, but I don't know what to do. Can you help me with the design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Of course! Discussing design options with customers is one of our favorite parts of the job. We'll walk through your space with you, talk about what you want each room to feel like, and recommend the best layout, fixture types, and placement.

mainEntity.name: Do you have any hidden fees?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope! Our technicians understand the importance of upfront pricing. What you see on the invoice is what you get. If any changes are made to your project, we will update it promptly and send it over for you to review.

mainEntity.name: Are there any services you don't offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: We do most electrical work, but not all. Services we don't currently offer include generator installs, solar installs, hanging christmas/bistro lights, standing lamp repairs, ethernet/data wiring, and thermostats.

mainEntity.name: Can you tell me more about your business?

acceptedAnswer.text: We have been in business for over 7 years and take pride in being a local, family-run business in Mesa, Arizona. Our customers' happiness and our quality of work are our number one priorities. We are licensed, bonded, and insured (ROC #365306). We believe being a small business allows us to offer a more personalized experience for our customers.

mainEntity.name: Do you warranty your work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we do. We offer a 2-year warranty on services we provide. Contact us for full warranty details.

mainEntity.name: Can you refer me to someone for a non-electrical project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! We are happy to provide referrals for other services. Over the years we've built relationships with great contractors across the Phoenix valley in plumbing, HVAC, roofing, and more. Just ask and we'll point you in the right direction.

mainEntity.name: How much does an electrician cost per hour in Phoenix?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many electricians in the Phoenix area charge between $75 and $150 per hour. At The Wire Guy Electric, we use flat-rate pricing instead. We quote you a price before we start and that's what you pay, whether the job takes one hour or three. We believe flat-rate pricing is the fairest approach because it puts the risk on us, not on you.

mainEntity.name: How much does an electrical panel upgrade cost in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Phoenix metro area, most electrical panel upgrades run between $1,800 and $3,500 for a standard 100-amp to 200-amp upgrade. Full service upgrades that include a new meter base, weatherhead, and panel typically range from $3,500 to $5,500 depending on the scope. Every home is different, so we recommend getting a free estimate for an accurate price.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to install recessed lighting?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a typical retrofit installation of six recessed LED lights in an existing room, most Phoenix valley homeowners can expect to pay between $800 and $1,500. That includes fixtures, wiring, switches, and labor. Price varies depending on ceiling accessibility, number of lights, and whether new circuits need to be run.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to install an EV charger at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Installing a Level 2 EV charger (240-volt) at a home in the Phoenix area typically costs between $500 and $1,500, depending on the distance from your panel to the charging location and whether your panel has capacity for a new circuit. If your panel needs an upgrade to support the charger, that adds to the cost. We install chargers for all makes and models.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my electrical panel needs to be upgraded?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include breakers that trip frequently, flickering lights when appliances kick on, a fuse box instead of a breaker panel, or a panel that's more than 25 years old. Homes with 100-amp panels running modern appliances and AC systems are usually overdue. We also strongly recommend replacing any Federal Pacific or Zinsco branded panels due to documented safety issues. We offer free estimates and will give you an honest answer.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a 100 amp and 200 amp electrical panel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 100-amp panel was standard in older homes and works for smaller properties with basic electrical needs. A 200-amp panel is the current standard and supports modern demands like central AC, electric dryers, pool pumps, EV chargers, and multiple large appliances. Most Phoenix valley homes built before the early 2000s have 100-amp panels. If you're adding major appliances or remodeling, upgrading to 200 amps is usually the smart move.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for electrical work in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most electrical work beyond basic repairs, yes. Panel upgrades, new circuit installations, rewiring, and EV charger installations all require a permit and inspection in Maricopa County. At The Wire Guy Electric, we handle the entire permit process for you. Any electrician who suggests skipping the permit is someone you should avoid.

mainEntity.name: What is a whole house surge protector and do I need one?

acceptedAnswer.text: A whole house surge protector installs at your electrical panel and protects every circuit from voltage spikes caused by lightning, utility grid fluctuations, or your AC unit cycling. In Arizona, monsoon season is a real threat to electronics and appliances. For the cost, typically $300 to $600 installed, it's one of the best investments you can make to protect thousands of dollars worth of equipment.

mainEntity.name: How often should I have my home's electrical system inspected?

acceptedAnswer.text: We recommend a professional electrical inspection every 5 to 10 years, or anytime you purchase a new home. If your home is more than 25 years old, an inspection is especially important. We also recommend one if you're experiencing flickering lights, warm outlets, or tripping breakers. Our inspections cover your panel, wiring, outlets, grounding, and overall system safety.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of bad electrical wiring in a house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Watch for flickering or dimming lights, burning smells near outlets or switches, discolored or warm outlet covers, frequently tripping breakers, buzzing sounds from walls or your panel, and outlets that don't work. Older Phoenix area homes, especially those built in the 1960s and 1970s, sometimes have aluminum wiring that can be a fire hazard if not properly maintained.

mainEntity.name: Is aluminum wiring dangerous? Should I replace it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Aluminum wiring was commonly used in homes built during the 1960s and 1970s. It's not inherently dangerous, but it requires more attention than copper. Aluminum expands and contracts more with heat, which can loosen connections and create fire hazards. The good news is you don't always need a full rewire. In many cases, we can install special connectors at every connection point to make your aluminum wiring safe.

mainEntity.name: Why does my breaker keep tripping?

acceptedAnswer.text: A breaker trips when the circuit is overloaded, meaning too many devices are drawing power from the same circuit. It can also trip from a short circuit or a ground fault. If a breaker trips repeatedly or immediately after you reset it, that's a sign of a more serious issue like a short in the wiring or a failing appliance. Don't ignore it. Give us a call and we can troubleshoot the issue.

mainEntity.name: Can I install an EV charger myself or do I need an electrician?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a licensed electrician. Installing a Level 2 EV charger requires running a dedicated 240-volt circuit from your panel, which involves working inside your breaker panel. It requires a permit and inspection in Arizona, and doing it incorrectly can damage your vehicle's charging system or create a fire hazard. We install chargers for every major EV brand and handle the permit process.

mainEntity.name: What type of recessed lights should I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: For homes in Arizona, we recommend IC-rated LED recessed fixtures. IC stands for Insulation Contact, meaning the fixture safely touches ceiling insulation without creating a fire risk. LED fixtures use less energy, produce almost no heat, and last 25,000 to 50,000 hours. For color temperature, most homeowners prefer 3000K for a warm, comfortable feel.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to install recessed lighting?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a typical room with 4 to 6 lights and attic access above, the install usually takes about half a day. Larger projects or rooms without attic access may take a full day. We always try to be efficient and clean up after ourselves so there's minimal disruption to your home.

mainEntity.name: Can you add outlets or circuits to my home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Adding outlets, dedicated circuits, and upgrading electrical capacity is one of the most common things we do. Whether you need a dedicated 240-volt outlet for a dryer, a new circuit for a home office, or additional outlets in any room, we can handle it. All new circuit work requires a permit in Maricopa County, and we take care of the entire process.

mainEntity.name: How do I choose a good electrician in Phoenix?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for someone who is licensed, bonded, and insured. Verify their license on the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) website. Read Google reviews and pay attention to patterns in the feedback. Ask if they offer free estimates and flat-rate pricing. Make sure they pull permits for jobs that require them. At The Wire Guy Electric, our ROC license number is 365306 and you can verify it anytime at azroc.gov.

This protects you as the homeowner because our work is backed by the state's contractor recovery fund, and our insurance covers any accidents or damage on the job.

acceptedAnswer.text: Our regular office hours are Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM. If you have an urgent situation, give us a call at 602-769-7892 and we'll do our best to accommodate you.
